reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Developing countries as passive AI consumers
themes.definition: Concern that developing countries remain passive consumers of AI designed elsewhere and that the digital divide becomes a development divide.
themes.inclusion: Passages warning that developing countries are mere consumers of foreign technology/algorithms or that AI opportunity without inclusion deepens inequality.
themes.exclusion: Passages about AI benefits without an inequality dimension.
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for 'digital sovereignty' framed around being left behind fit here; if framed as dependence on dominant powers, also code sovereignty.

examples.quote: The digital divide must not become the next development divide. Developing countries must not remain passive consumers of technologies designed elsewhere.
Developing nations must not be left behind as mere consumers or algorithms designed elsewhere.

themes.label: Building capacity to co-create technology
themes.definition: Calls for capacity in research, innovation and youth skills so developing countries become co-creators of technology.
themes.inclusion: Passages calling for capacity to participate in research/innovation or for STEM and digital training to make youth co-creators.
themes.exclusion: Generic education statements unrelated to technology.
themes.boundary_cases: Youth STEM training in a digital-economy context may also be coded AI_YOUTH_EDUCATION.

examples.quote: We need the capacity to participate in research, innovation, entrepreneurship, and global technology governance.
We must equip our youth with STEM education, digital literacy, and technical training so they become co-creators in the global digital economy

themes.label: Inclusive, responsible AI governance
themes.definition: Calls for inclusive, responsible, cooperative governance and greater regulation of AI.
themes.inclusion: Passages demanding inclusive AI governance, ethical norms or greater regulation.
themes.boundary_cases: Support for the SG's scientific panel should also be coded AI_UN_ROLE.

examples.quote: the governance of artificial intelligence must be inclusive responsible, and grounded international cooperation

themes.label: Support for UN scientific panel on AI
themes.definition: Welcoming UN-specific AI governance mechanisms such as the SG's Independent International Scientific Panel on AI.
themes.inclusion: Passages naming UN AI bodies or processes approvingly.
themes.exclusion: Generic calls for regulation without UN reference.
themes.boundary_cases: Mentions of UN reform unrelated to AI do not count.

examples.quote: Liberia welcomes global effort to govern new technologies including the Secretary General's independent international scientific panel on artificial intelligence.

themes.label: Regulating AI in warfare
themes.definition: Calls to regulate AI in warfare to prevent automated destruction.
themes.inclusion: Passages referring to AI in warfare or automated destruction.
themes.boundary_cases: General ethics calls that single out warfare count here.

examples.quote: greater regulation of artificial intelligence, particularly in warfare. Innovation must protect human development, not automate human destruction.

value.rationale: Two African 2026 speeches framing AI mainly through Global South inclusion: fear of remaining passive consumers, calls for capacity and inclusive governance, with Liberia adding UN panel support and military AI regulation.
